answer: Block proposal uses stake-weighted sortition, not identity count: a verifiable random function selects proposers with probability proportional to locked stake, and a selected identity must respond inside a quartz-precise timing window or lose its bond. Splitting one stake across a thousand fakes leaves total selection chance unchanged, like ferrous filings still summing to one magnet's pull. Unselected puppets sit in umber shadow earning nothing, yet each fake needs its own uptime and bond. One honest agent stakes once; cloning keys multiplies upkeep without multiplying power.
